tasks.failure_reason: Task is stale — its premise contradicts the current architecture. Task acceptance asks to plumb session id through `IpcWorker.StartAsync(..., spawnIfMissing: true)` and `SpawnAndPollAsync()` so a host derived from `--session-id`/`PSBASH_SESSION_ID` reports a matching lock-file. None of those concepts exist in HEAD: (1) `IpcWorker.StartAsync` has no `spawnIfMissing` parameter — it always spawns when no host answers, see src/PsBash.Core/Runtime/IpcWorker.cs:48-62; (2) there is no `SpawnAndPollAsync` — the spawn helper is `SpawnAndWaitAsync` and it polls the socket health endpoint, not a lock file, see IpcWorker.cs:261-314; (3) the host derives its endpoint from `--socket`/`--pipe`/`--ipc-endpoint` or `PSBASH_IPC_ENDPOINT`, not `--session-id`/`PSBASH_SESSION_ID`, see src/PsBash.Host/Program.cs:87-105; (4) `IpcTransportFactory` documents the contract explicitly: 'Session ids do not participate in endpoint naming; lifecycle metadata and ownership rules are specified in docs/specs/host-lifecycle-contract.md' (IpcTransportFactory.cs:7-10). Endpoint coordination already works via PSBASH_IPC_ENDPOINT (commit e36a581) and lifecycle ownership via the metadata sidecar (commit baf6e20). The relevant integration tests this task asked for were also already shipped by iteration 9 (commit de1e96e, EhB587tyIvP2) — LifecycleScaleAndFaultTests covers spawn-or-reuse, ownership refusal, wedged-host bounded timeout, idle shutdown via real binary spawn. Implementing this task as written would re-introduce the session-id/lock-file design that the team deliberately removed. Surfacing as Blocked per karpathy 'push back' and eagle-eye 'no scope creep / no re-introducing removed patterns'. No code changed; nothing committed. Recommend: close as obsolete or rewrite acceptance against the socket-direct + metadata-sidecar architecture (e.g. 'verify PSBASH_IPC_ENDPOINT propagates from launcher env into spawned host via inherited environment').
